findings.reason: The protected source is the canonical dense-array plus value-to-position map design. It handles duplicate insertion and missing removal directly, performs swap deletion without a special last-element branch, and delegates uniform selection to random.choice over the dense members. The implementation is concise and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 380 and its Python RandomizedSet surface. The Reference preserves all three operations, their Boolean semantics, the average-O(1) requirement, uniform random choice, the nonempty getRandom guarantee, the source example with its complete explanation, and all three constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064650026. Its array and map state, insertion, swap deletion, and random selection are preserved exactly in the protected app-local class; solve is only the required operation-stream adapter.

The legal 128, 1024, and 8192 tiers span 64x in set size and exercise equal batches of insertion and arbitrary removal within the total-call limit. The current source passes all 11 executions at +0.01 relative growth and 0.96x; a correct list-only design passes every benchmark output but fails only scaling at +0.31.

The Approach accurately derives the dense array and inverse map, explains the swap-delete invariant including removal of the final element, justifies uniform probability, describes state-aware validation, and states average O(1) operations with O(n) space.

The hash-bound public Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including the full API, uniformity and complexity requirements, the sole source example and its nondeterministic step, the signed-value range, total-call limit, and nonempty-random-call guarantee.
